title: Revenue-detail scope: pp.127-140 double-count the spine unless the scope axis is decided
description:
Mapping pp.127-140 the obvious way publishes DOUBLE the city's General Fund
revenue, and every check stays green. This bead must be decided before any YAML
is written for fisc-5gk.1.

THE MECHANISM

internal/project/sankey.go:545 keys cells on (kind, category, fundGroup).
data/taxonomy.yaml holds 25 slugs, ALL category-level -- there is no slug for a
revenue line item. So each of p127's thirteen property-tax detail rows must
carry category: taxes/property, fund_group: general, which is the SAME cellKey
as the p66 spine fact. netCells sums them.

They are the same money. Verified:
  p0066.txt:13  Property Taxes (General Fund) FY2025-26 = 64,143,762
  p0127.txt:37  Total Property Taxes          FY2025-26 = 64,143,762

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT

- headline-ties-to-facts and link-values-tie-to-facts tie the graph to the facts
  it was built FROM, not to the document.
- Build-time CheckTotals is per-part; the p66 part and the p127 part each pass
  against their own printed totals.
- The result is a plausible wrong value, which is the exact defect class this
  project exists to prevent.

THE TWO OPTIONS, BOTH WITH A COST

(a) scope: all-funds-gross -- silently doubles GF revenue. Unacceptable.
(b) A new scope string -- facts-are-projected (internal/check/coverage.go:98-127)
    then FAILS unless the scope is added to unprojectedScopes (coverage.go:25,
    currently empty). That is a Go change, not a YAML change.

coverage.go's own doc comment records the precedent: "Moving twenty facts to a
mistyped `all-funds-gross-detail` took over half the city's revenue out of the
published chart, and every check still passed."

WHAT THIS BEAD MUST SETTLE

- the scope string for revenue detail;
- whether line items get their own taxonomy slugs or a sub-category axis;
- how the detail RECONCILES AGAINST the spine rather than adding to it.

This is the revenue lane's counterpart to fisc-28s and fisc-o15, which the
department lane has and this lane did not. Found in peer review of the landing
plan, 2026-08-18.
acceptance_criteria: the scope string is decided and recorded here; line-item identity (own slugs vs sub-category axis) is decided; the detail reconciles against the spine rather than summing with it; a test asserts the published GF property-tax figure is 64,143,762 and NOT 128,287,524

title: Structural remainder: cell relocation and dropped-column detection
description:
fisc-1wr.5 lands in two pieces. The parent's artifact/registry drift and the cross-language Normalize agreement are implementable at spine-only coverage and land in Wave A. These two want a settled resolver, so they land after the geometry column guard (fisc-yqv.2) and the coverage lanes.

CELL RELOCATION -- independently re-resolve each fact by its identity tuple (doc_id, rule_id, row_path, row_label, column_path, fiscal_year, basis) and assert the resolved position equals the recorded one. This is the check that replaced a tautological earlier draft: hashing a fact's token and then asserting the token matches can never fail. Asking the RULES where that cell is TODAY is a question the committed file cannot answer for itself. Two outcomes worth distinguishing: an id absent from the re-resolved index means the cell this fact names no longer exists; an id present at a different page/offset/token means the table moved, and the finding names both positions.

Reuses the resolver memoization from fisc-uv6, so verify still resolves each part once rather than a third time.

DROPPED COLUMN -- if a page's text carries a longer numeric run on a mapped row's label line than the table has columns, fail with 'possible dropped column'. ACFR p34 loses one silently. Note this overlaps with fisc-yqv.2's column_headers, which catches a dropped column at resolve time; this catches it over already-built facts, which is the case where the rules were not re-run.
acceptance_criteria: a fact whose row moved is reported with both positions and is distinguishable from a fact whose cell no longer exists; the relocation pass adds no additional resolve of any part; ACFR p34's shape is a test case
notes:
2026-08-18 NOTE from fisc-yqv.2. This bead's dropped-column half cites ACFR p34
as the page that loses a column silently, and says the overlap with
fisc-yqv.2's column_headers is that the resolver catches it at resolve time
while this catches it over already-built facts.

Measured: ACFR p34 is one of the 124 pages where the -layout line structure and
the geometry clustering disagree, so the resolver's column guard can NEVER run
there. It refuses the page rather than catching the drop. The overlap is smaller
than it looks and this bead is the only thing that would catch ACFR p34's shape.
See fisc-gmx.
2026-08-18 DEFERRED, landing plan -- but revisit immediately after fisc-5gk.2. Cell relocation is worth little over 240 facts from 2 pages; after both coverage lanes land there are roughly 1,580 facts across 18 more pages, which is when 'independently re-resolve each fact and assert the position matches' starts earning its keep. This bead's own note calls it the only thing that would catch ACFR p34's shape.

title: Re-anchor the spine: 7 anchor edits across 5 of 10 parts
description:
The claim that -layout lets the section_ordinal/stop_at workarounds go is WRONG. section_ordinal: 4 is still needed (still four occurrences of 'FY 2026-27'); stop_at: '$' is still needed (p67 still prints no TOTAL REVENUES: label); and 'line anchors' describes a resolver feature that does not exist -- anchor is a raw strings.Index (resolve.go:206) and nothing in internal/mapping is line-aware.

What breaks, all fail-closed, 5 of 10 parts:
1. MULTI-SPACE HEADER ANCHORS (3 parts: spine-expenditures p67, spine-transfers-out p67, spine-fund-balance p67). -layout prints 'Capital Funds' + 15 spaces + 'Debt Service Funds'; the single-spaced section string no longer occurs. Re-anchor to section: 'Internal Service Funds', section_ordinal: 2.
2. PAGE FOOTERS (4 parts). xberg's strip_repeating_text deleted them; -layout emits 'BUDGET FY 2025-27      Page 62'. Every part with no stop_at now swallows it. The footer carries a bare '62' which amount.Parse accepts as $62, so this is corpus-wide: every 'runs to end of page' part needs an explicit stop_at.

The mapping file's ~80-line prose preamble describes the xberg single-line shape throughout and needs rewriting, not patching.
acceptance_criteria: 240 facts, 24 columns tied, every amount_cents identical to the pre-migration values
notes: DONE (working tree, uncommitted). 7 anchor edits across 5 of 10 parts, exactly as the bead predicted. (1) spine-expenditures p67, (2) spine-transfers-out p67, (3) spine-fund-balance p67: section 'Capital Funds Debt Service Funds Special Revenue Funds Internal Service Funds' -> 'Internal Service Funds\n', section_ordinal 2 unchanged. The bead's suggested fix was right but incomplete: the trailing newline matters, because it turns 'the last name on the header line' from a hope into a claim -- without it a fifth fund group would resolve to a start mid-header, with it the anchor disappears and fails closed. (4) spine-transfers-out p66, (5) spine-transfers-out p67, (6) spine-fund-balance p66, (7) spine-fund-balance p67: added stop_at 'BUDGET FY 2025-27'. section_ordinal 4 and stop_at '$' both re-verified as still required: p67 prints 'FY 2026-27' exactly 4 times and 'TOTAL REVENUES:' zero times. ~80-line preamble rewritten, not patched. PROOF: 240 facts / 240 distinct ids / sum(amount_cents)=255588874000, id sequence and every amount_cents byte-identical to HEAD baseline; only offset (all 240) and token (10, all '\\-' -> '-' zero cells on p67 capital FY2027) differ. 4 of 10 parts tie, 24 columns, parts_unchecked unchanged at the 6 no-total_row parts. All 240 offsets land on their token in the new page file and every token is a whole whitespace-delimited page token (no fragments). All five control totals re-derive by hand from the new page text. fisc export reproduces sankey.golden.json byte for byte apart from metadata.generated_by. go test ./... green, golangci-lint 0 issues, gofmt clean. Also corrected now-false prose in internal/mapping/rule.go (SectionOrdinal doc claimed the schedule is on one line of extracted text), testdata/README.md and docs/agents/conventions.md. Cannot bd close: blocked by open fisc-yqv.3.

Three p67 parts moved off a spelled-out header string (-layout spaces it 14/15/9 on one half and 15/14/9 on the other) to section: 'Internal Service Funds\n' + ordinal 2. Four parts with no stop_at gained one: the running footer 'BUDGET FY 2025-27  Page 62' carries a bare 62 that amount.Parse accepts as $62. title: Rewrite tools/extract.py on poppler; re-extract all three docs
description:
poppler-utils replaces xberg in requirements.txt.

KEEP (load-bearing): sorted output, canonical JSON, atomic writes, clean_output of stale files before writing, and the rule that Python never reads data/sources.yaml (two parties recording the sha256 independently is a real check).

DROP (xberg shape): xberg_version, config, config_sha256, table_count, pages_with_tables, NORMALIZER_VERSION.

NEW ANSWER NEEDED: poppler has no structured error channel. It writes 'Syntax Warning: Bad annotation destination' to stderr and exits 0. Record the poppler version and captured stderr per document; do not claim manifest.errors works as before.

PUBLISH PAGE TEXT AS .txt NOT .md: GitHub renders .md in the blob view and collapses the runs of spaces that ARE the grid, which would silently break the provenance deep links fisc-gxa.5 depends on. Carry the rename through corpus.go:217, export/page.go:311, site/app.js:282, export_test.go:197, and the now-false comments at corpus.go:219 and rule.go:30.
close_reason: extract.py rewritten on poppler 24.02.0, stdlib only. All 786 pages re-extracted; byte-identical across runs, locales, and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH/PYTHONHASHSEED. Determinism verified by a third party on an independent re-run. schema_version bumped to 2 on both sides after review found that leaving it at 1 made a broken reader SILENT: Open() succeeded, then Page(n) returned ErrNotFound, which corpus.go documents as the normal 'no such page' case. Bumping it surfaced a real latent bug -- corpus.SchemaVersion was validating both the manifest and each table JSON, two independent contracts sharing one constant. poppler has no structured error channel; stderr is captured per invocation and the docstring says plainly that an empty errors list is not a promise every page came out whole.

title: Column-position guard in the resolver
description:
With geometry available, a value must fall within its column's x-range, derived from the header line. This is the actual payoff of the extractor switch: adopting a layout-preserving extractor and then reading it with a whitespace tokenizer (tokens(), resolve.go:744, which records byte offset only and no column position) throws away the reason for switching.

Without this guard the sparse pages produce plausible wrong values rather than errors.
acceptance_criteria: a row whose 2nd column is blank and 3rd carries a figure resolves the figure to column 3 or fails closed -- never silently to column 2; CIP p40 PB200654 fails closed naming the row
notes:
2026-08-18 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA AMENDED. The original read, verbatim:

  "a row whose 2nd column is blank and 3rd carries a figure resolves the figure
  to column 3 or fails closed -- never silently to column 2; CIP p40 PB200654
  reads correctly"

The last clause is unmeetable and this bead's own notes already said why: six of
PB200654's eight cells print a "-" that is in NO substrate, because they are
drawn as non-text. No column guard recovers a mark the PDF never wrote. Closing
on "reads correctly" would have published a false claim, so the clause moved to
fisc-8ln (whose AC lost its "or fails closed" escape in the same edit, or the
obligation would have belonged to no open bead).

The first clause is met in its fails-closed branch, which is the only branch this
lane can demonstrate: geometry is a pure CROSS-CHECK here and never selects which
tokens a row consumes, so a blank cell yields a refusal rather than a correctly
placed figure. "Resolves the figure to column 3" needs band-driven selection,
which is filed with the sparse relaxation.

WHAT LANDED, in six commits: internal/geom (leaf, stdlib only); corpus.Doc.Geometry;
the doc interface at three methods; the verbatim-copy fixture tables generalised
to {document, artifact} over both substrates; column_headers on Part with per-part,
per-page and cross-file validation; the guard itself in internal/mapping/geometry.go;
and column_headers on all ten published spine parts.

DEVIATIONS FROM THE DESIGN ON THIS BEAD, each with its evidence:

(1) The count guard was NOT relaxed. The design said geometry "NECESSARILY
relaxes" positionalValues' exact len(toks) == ExpectedValues. That is true of
SPARSE pages and no mapped part is sparse: p66's data lines carry four value
words each and p67's carry eight, on all 24 of them, dashes included. Relaxing
would have traded the guard that caught fisc-c00 for a replacement exercised only
by the dense pages that never needed it.

(2) The gutter is the FIRST COLUMN HEADER'S x0, not the midpoint to the label
header. The design's own counterexamples refute the design: CIP p40's wrap word
"and" ends at 228.6 and CIP p29's "REVITILIZATION" at 234.85, both RIGHT of the
midpoints (213.16 and 218.67), so both would have filed into band 0. First-header-x0
(238.87 and 245.10) excludes them and keeps every real value, including the bare
leading "$" glyphs. Clearances are thin on CIP and are recorded in the code:
9.46pt left and 3.81pt right on p40.

(3) No column_headers_ordinal. The full ordered header sequence occurs exactly
once page-wide on 66, 67, 127, 128-140, 167, 168, 169, 170, CIP 40 and CIP 29 --
with zero unconsumed words right of the first match on every one. Shipping five
validation branches and a selection branch that no fixture can reach, inside the
guard everything else is about to trust, was the worse trade. Ambiguity is a
refusal naming the candidate lines. Filed for when a page forces it.

(4) No geom.ErrNoGeometry sentinel. corpus.ErrNotFound already means "the
manifest does not list this artifact", and a second sentinel would have put the
artifact reader's vocabulary in the leaf that exists so mapping need not import it.

(5) Substrate agreement is BYTE equality, not the design's "normalized text".
Normalizing would paper over a genuine disagreement, and the point of a second
witness is that it is allowed to disagree.

MEASUREMENTS THE DESIGN GOT WRONG, corrected here:

- Filing by header overlap misfiles 19-30 "on the mapped pages" -- it misfiles
  ZERO on pp.66/67. Over the eight measured pages the two rules disagree on 24
  tokens: 19 zero dashes (p127, p167, p168, p169, CIP p40), 2 bare "$" glyphs and
  3 footer tokens. The doc comment and TestOverlapFilingLosesZeroDashes carry the
  corrected figure.
- The line-grouping 1:1 with -layout is NOT a corpus property. It fails on 124 of
  786 pages, and 99 more fail token agreement. No page in current or near-term
  scope fails either, and the guard refuses the rest rather than reading them
  approximately. Do not write a corpus-wide assertion of it; it is false.
- p67 has 33 non-blank lines but 24 DATA lines.

fisc-j5p's hypothesis was disproved and is recorded on that bead.
close_reason:
The column guard is live over the published citywide spine, and all 240 facts and
facts/facts.jsonl are byte-identical with it on -- what changed is what is
checked, not what is published.

Six commits: internal/geom (leaf, stdlib only, the -bbox reader and the band
model); corpus.Doc.Geometry; the mapping doc interface at three methods, with the
argument for a required method over a type assertion written down; both
verbatim-copy fixture tests generalised to {document, artifact} tables over both
substrates; column_headers on Part with per-part, per-page and cross-file
validation; the guard in internal/mapping/geometry.go; column_headers on all ten
published spine parts; and the CIP p29/p40 tests.

Evidence: spineFacts 240 and spineTiedColumns 24 with the guard on, every balance
identity and headline figure unmoved, facts.jsonl and sankey.golden.json
byte-identical, fisc verify 19 passed 0 failed.

The guard is not inert, and that is asserted rather than hoped: a rule that names
only the last three of p66's four printed headers is refused naming the row, the
token, its x-position and the column the page actually prints it in; a header pair
in the wrong order is refused as an order claim; a part one column short of the
page is refused because the header line carries a header no column claims; and a
one-column part whose two rows were fused onto one printed line is caught by the
line count, which is the case no other check can see.

AC amended and the original preserved in the notes above, along with the five
deviations from the design and the three measurements on this bead that turned
out to be wrong. Follow-ups filed: fisc-gmx (substrate disagreement, 223 of 786
pages), band-driven selection with the sparse count relaxation, StatedTotals'
substrate inconsistency, column_headers_ordinal, and the two-grid page.

title: Emit both -layout text and -bbox geometry
description:
pdftotext -layout alone CANNOT distinguish an empty cell from an absent one: on a sparse wide grid a blank cell yields no token at all. CIP p40 row PB200654 prints two figures with six blanks between and -layout gives exactly two tokens. labelledValues takes toks[:ncols] (resolve.go:378), so a figure silently lands in the wrong column -- a plausible wrong value, which is what this project fails closed on, and it makes 'absent is not zero' unenforceable. xberg's tables/*.json grid was the only artifact carrying that geometry, and pp.131-140 / pp.167-170 (the Stage 2 targets) are the sparse ones.

-bbox is also the only way to keep one existing claim reproducible: the mapping file justifies its corrected omitted_rows: [] on p67 with 'pdftotext -bbox puts ten revenue rows here at the same ten y-positions' -- the fisc-c00 evidence.

Emit pages/pNNNN.txt (-layout) plus geometry/pNNNN.json (word boxes from -bbox). Strictly more useful than xberg's tables; replaces them rather than sitting beside them.
acceptance_criteria: geometry/pNNNN.json carries per-word text + bbox for every page of all three docs; a sparse-grid page (CIP p40) can be read column-correctly using it
notes: 2026-08-18 CORRECTION, from peer review of the landing plan. This bead's premise that pp.131-140 and pp.167-170 'are the sparse ones' is measurably FALSE. All 18 pages in that scope were checked against the emitted -bbox geometry: every data row carries exactly 4 value tokens, with '-' printed in every zero cell. They are uniformly dense. The -bbox substrate and the column guard built on it (fisc-yqv.2) are therefore not justified by any page currently in scope -- the poppler migration itself (fisc-yqv.3) IS, and demonstrably worked (p130 recovered 13 rows xberg lost). Recording the distinction so the guard's cost is not retro-justified by the extractor's success.
close_reason: Emits pages/pNNNN.txt (-layout) + geometry/pNNNN.json (-bbox word boxes), replacing tables/. Geometry verified sufficient for column identity: CIP p40 PB202617's lone 500,000 at x=391.1 sits under FY 2026-27 (369.9-418.9), where a whitespace read would have filed it under FY 2024-25. Word encoding flattened to [x0,y0,x1,y1,text] after review: 18.7 -> 8.2 MiB, 41.3 bytes/word. Geometry does NOT recover a value absent from the text layer -- see fisc-8ln.

title: [epic] E0 Extraction replacement: pdftotext replaces xberg
description:
The committed xberg artifacts have silently lost data rows on exactly the pages the POC needs: PDF p167 prints a ~40-line department x object grid and pages/p0167.md retains 7; p130 prints 13 Miscellaneous Revenue detail rows and p0130.md retains 0. This is the fisc-c00 failure class, and Part.OmittedRows' doc comment forbids absorbing it in a rule -- if rows go missing between the PDF and the artifact, fix extraction.

A scratch migration replacing all 786 pages with pdftotext -layout output confirmed: all 240 spine facts reproduce with identical amount_cents AND identical ids, sankey.json matches the golden except its build stamp, all 24 columns still tie, every headline control total re-derives, output is byte-identical across runs and locales. Of 583 grouped-value tokens xberg produced that -layout does not, every one is an xberg corruption (dash-glued negatives, split digits, a lost decimal).

Ends with all three docs re-extracted, the spine re-anchored, and the money proven identical cell by cell.

Verified in peer review of the landing plan that the rewrite did what it was for: p130's 13 Miscellaneous Revenue rows, of which xberg retained 0, are all present in the poppler artifact. One correction recorded on fisc-yqv.1: its premise that pp.131-140 and 167-170 'are the sparse ones' is measurably false -- all 18 pages carry exactly 4 value tokens per row.

title: StatedTotals cannot read a totals row glued to the next data row
description:
Budget Book p67's expenditure totals cannot be read. The extracted page puts the TOTAL EXPENDITURES row and the TRANSFER OUT row on ONE physical line:

  ... 1,070,500 1,115,510 $1,061,355 $969,934 $6,984,597 $6,969,898 $19,267,561 $11,808,000 $25,077,367 $26,544,515 28,584,740 36,047,736 - - 1,137,050 900,550 40,000 612,000

StatedTotals anchors a label-less part on stop_at ('$') and asks amountRun for the first MAXIMAL run of exactly len(columns) parsable amounts within that line. Sixteen amounts follow the anchor -- the 8 totals plus the 8 transfer-out figures -- so the maximal run is 16, never 8, and the read fails with ErrNotFound.

That is indistinguishable from 'the totals row moved', which is a genuine hard failure, so it cannot be waved through. p67's revenue totals (line 15) and total-sources (line 17) each have exactly 8 amounts after their anchor, which is why only this one part fails.

The document already distinguishes the two rows typographically: totals rows are $-prefixed and data rows are bare. internal/mapping/testdata/spine.yaml relies on that convention already ('the totals row is the first line whose figures are prefixed with $ -- every data row above it is bare'). The resolver does not use it.
design:
In amountRun, when a maximal run is not the wanted length AND the run begins with a $-prefixed token, also consider that run's $-prefixed PREFIX. Return it if it is exactly the wanted length.

Deliberately additive: the existing maximal-run result is computed first and preferred, so a line the resolver reads today reads identically. The new branch can only turn a failure into a success. That rules out a regression on the pages where totals are only partially $-marked, which fail closed as before.
acceptance_criteria: p67's spine-expenditures part ties its 8 column totals; p66's labelled totals and p67's revenue totals are unchanged; a line whose $-prefixed prefix is the wrong width still fails.
close_reason: Fixed: amountRun considers a run's $-prefixed prefix when the maximal run is the wrong width. Deliberately additive -- the maximal run is computed and preferred first, so every line that read before reads identically and the new branch can only turn a failure into a success. p67 spine-expenditures now ties its 8 columns; the spine ties 24 of 24. Regression test TestCurrencyMarkedTotalsRunSurvivesAGluedDataRow covers the glued line, a wrong-width $-prefix, and an unchanged bare run.

title: Extraction dropped a data row: xberg strip_repeating_text eats identical rows
description:
Budget Book PDF p67 prints TEN revenue rows; data/extracted/.../pages/p0067.md carried only NINE (72 tokens where 10 rows x 8 columns = 80). Verified with 'pdftotext -bbox -f 67 -l 67': p67's revenue rows sit at y = 194, 210, 226, 241, 257, 273, 289, 304, 320, 336 -- the SAME ten y-positions as p66's ten labelled rows. The document omits nothing.

Rows 8-10 (Sales Taxes, Fines & Forfeitures, Licenses & Permits) are three consecutive all-dash lines. xberg's content_filter.strip_repeating_text defaults to true; it is a header/footer dedup heuristic and it treated the third identical DATA row as repeating boilerplate. Setting content_filter.strip_repeating_text=false restores all three (80 tokens, verified).

This matters far beyond one row. The project had recorded the loss as a property of the DOCUMENT -- docs/m0-spike.md finding #4, the omitted_rows comment in internal/mapping/testdata/spine.yaml, the OmittedRows doc comment in internal/mapping/rule.go, and fisc-mq4.7's own description all say p67 'omits' an all-zero row. It does not. Declaring it via Part.OmittedRows ('rows absent from THIS part') would launder a pipeline defect into a permanent published assertion about the City's budget, and row_label is inside fact.MakeID, so the affected facts would carry a coin-flip label.

The resolver's positional count guard (internal/mapping/resolve.go positionalValues) was CORRECTLY firing. It is the only reason this was caught.
design: Add content_filter: {strip_repeating_text: false} to CONFIG in tools/extract.py and bump EXTRACTOR_VERSION. CONFIG is hashed into manifest.config_sha256, so the change is attributable. Review the full-corpus artifact diff before committing: strip_repeating_text is a global heuristic and any other page it was silently editing will also change. include_headers/include_footers stay false and are separate knobs.
acceptance_criteria: p0067.md revenue block tokenizes to 80 between the 4th 'FY 2026-27' and the first '$'; omitted_rows disappears from the spine rule entirely; the four places that record the false premise are corrected; artifact diff outside the affected pages is reviewed and explained.
close_reason: Fixed in 6806ec7: content_filter.strip_repeating_text=False, EXTRACTOR_VERSION=2, corpus regenerated. p67 revenue block is 80 tokens (10 rows x 8). Zero numeric tokens lost corpus-wide; 326 pages gained restored content. Four records of the false premise corrected (m0-spike.md, testdata/spine.yaml, rule.go OmittedRows doc, testdata/README.md) plus this bead's parent fisc-mq4.7. Regression guard: TestExtractionDropOutIsNotAnOmission.

title: Rebuild-and-diff facts.jsonl in CI
description: CI runs 'fisc build -o $(mktemp -d)' and byte-compares the result against the committed facts.jsonl. Without this, a hand-edited facts.jsonl passes CI and the deployed site is built from different numbers than the audit trail -- the one thing a provenance gate must prevent. Pure Go, so it costs nothing and preserves the no-LFS-in-CI property.
notes: 2026-08-17 IMPLEMENTATION DEVIATION, deliberate: the description says 'fisc build -o $(mktemp -d)', which the tool refuses by design -- --output is resolved against the repository root and validateRepoPath (pkg/cmd/build/build.go:130) rejects absolute paths. The CI job builds to bin/facts-rebuilt.jsonl instead (bin/ is gitignored and make clean already owns it, so the rebuild leaves the tree exactly as checked out) and compares with cmp, not 'git diff --exit-code'. cmp because git diff compares through the .gitattributes 'text eol=lf' clean filter rather than the bytes, and because the git diff form would leave the committed fact store overwritten in the workspace on failure. Recorded so the next reader does not 'fix' it back toward the description.
close_reason: The facts job rebuilds to bin/facts-rebuilt.jsonl and byte-compares with cmp against the committed facts/facts.jsonl. Deviation from the description's literal 'fisc build -o $(mktemp -d)' recorded in the notes -- the tool refuses absolute output paths by design.

title: Structural checks: drift, cell relocation, dropped column
description:
- artifact drift: any data/extracted file whose sha256 differs from its manifest entry; any manifest whose source_sha256 differs from the registry; any manifest whose xberg_version differs from the pin
- registry drift (--full only): recomputed PDF sha256 vs sources.yaml
- CELL RELOCATION: independently re-resolve each fact by row_path + column_path and assert the resolved position equals the recorded one. This REPLACES a check that was tautological in an earlier draft -- hashing content and then asserting the content matched can never fail independently. A mismatch means the table shifted, which is precisely the event nothing else detects.
- dropped-column detection: if a page's text has a longer numeric run on a mapped row's label line than the table has columns, fail with 'possible dropped column' (ACFR p34 loses a column silently)

Default verify needs NO PDFs and NO Python; --full adds registry drift and runs monthly with lfs: true.
notes:
ALSO: cross-language normalizer agreement. internal/amount.Normalize must produce the same output as normalize_cell in tools/extract.py, because the committed artifacts hash normalized text with the Python one and a Go reader that normalized differently would compute different hashes for identical content.

One divergence is known and deliberate: extract.py applies Unicode NFKC, Go does not (that would mean a golang.org/x/text dependency, byob-release.10, for a transform that changes nothing in this corpus -- all 382 committed tables hash identically either way). This check is what catches it if that stops being true. The Go doc comment on Normalize cites this bead.

ID = fisc-f-<12 hex of sha256(doc_id|rule_id|row_path|column_path|fiscal_year|basis)>, deliberately EXCLUDING amount_cents and any row/col index -- so a corrected amount is a modified line rather than delete+add, and an upstream row insertion does not renumber the file. ID = fisc-f-<12 hex of sha256(doc_id|rule_id|row_path|row_label|column_path|fiscal_year|basis)>, unit-separator joined so component boundaries cannot shift. row_label is in the tuple because row_path is NOT unique within a rule: p127 prints 13 detail lines all classified taxes/property, and taxonomy.yaml is explicit those are a label not a category -- review caught the collision and it is now a test. Why this is separate from the integrity hash: 16 ACFR tables are byte-identical duplicates of another (one 12-way group across pp.12-23; the Budget Book has a 20-way group), so a content hash is NOT an identity. Resolution must require a unique best match; ambiguity or no-match is a hard error printing the top three candidates with their pages and first rows, via ErrHint (byob-errors.2).

Text locator is {page, section, section_ordinal, stop_at}; ordinal is mandatory because REVENUES:/EXPENDITURES: each occur twice on p66. Table locator is {ordinal, label_fingerprint, bbox_centroid}, and a (page,ordinal) miss is always ErrNotFound -- never a fingerprint search that resolves elsewhere, since ACFR p12/p13 are identical in fingerprint, content hash AND bbox. title: Rule schema + parser (substrate: text|table|manual)
description:
Page text is the PRIMARY substrate: tables miss 46% of the Budget Book's money pages, including the spine (p66-67), the transfer schedule (p76), and revenue-by-fund (p127-140). Typed string enums, not iota, for anything crossing YAML/JSON (byob-typed-string-enums-sql).

 - a logical table can span pages, and the continuation page may carry NO row labels at all (p67 is a positional continuation of p66)
 - the continuation page OMITS rows that are all-zero across its columns, so a naive positional zip silently shifts every label after the gap. Rules need an explicit omitted_rows declaration plus a row-count assertion that fails loudly on mismatch.
 - column identity is (fund_group, fiscal_year), addressed by a column_path, not by a single header string (headers span two rows and Table.columns is always empty)

title: Row.Label cannot express a two-field row identity, so p76 can only be read by encoding the page's kerning
description:
A row's identity on Budget Book p76 is TWO printed fields with an arbitrary run
of spaces between them:

  Transfer From Low Income Hsng          to General Fund     257,012  -  -  -  (10)
  Transfer From Home Grant               to General Fund       8,932  8,706 ...

mapping.Row carries a single Label, matched by strings.Index as one substring
(resolve.go:460). Neither field alone works, and both failures are demonstrated
rather than argued:

- Label = the source only. The destination sits where the figures are expected
  and the read fails: `cannot parse amount "to"`.
- Label = the destination only. The source lands in the gap before the label,
  where checkGap refuses it as an unmapped row.

So the only label that resolves today is the two fields WITH THE EXACT SPACE RUN
between them -- 24 spaces on one row, 27 on the next -- which is the kerning of
one release encoded in a rule file. testdata/spine.yaml's own doctrine forbids
exactly this ("an anchor may not assume single spacing"), and it is right to:
the runs are typeset per row and per column half.

internal/mapping/testdata/transfers-p76.yaml does it anyway, deliberately and
with the reason in its header, because it is a reconciliation fixture pinned
against a byte-identical page copy. Nothing published may.

WANTED: a row whose label is two anchors with unconstrained whitespace between
them -- not a regex, and not a relaxation of the substring match, because the
gap has to stay checkable. Both parts are PUBLISHED text, so the fact's
row_label can still be the pair.

RELATED, and worth deciding together: fisc-0cs wants Row.Continuation for
wrapped labels. Both are the same shape of gap -- "a row's label is not one
contiguous substring" -- and p76 has one of each.

title: Band-driven cell selection: the sparse read, per-cell ErrAbsent, and the count relaxation
description:
fisc-yqv.2 landed geometry as a pure CROSS-CHECK: the -layout read is unchanged
and geometry only supplies a column index the read is checked against. That is
why turning it on moved no byte of facts.jsonl. It is also why a sparse row can
only be REFUSED, never read.

To read one, geometry has to SELECT the row's tokens -- take the words on the
row's printed line, assign each to a band, and let a band with no word be an
absent cell. Three things follow, and they are one change rather than three:

(1) positionalValues' exact len(toks) == ExpectedValues has to relax to <=, since
a sparse row legitimately produces fewer tokens. It must be gated on an explicit
per-part declaration -- do not relax it globally. A dense part keeps both guards
permanently. This is the guard that caught fisc-c00.

(2) With P5 relaxed, two checks become reachable that are dead today and were
deliberately left out rather than shipped unexercised: that no two rows read the
SAME printed line, and the line-count arm generally.

(3) A cell holding more than one word must be assembled, and the mechanic is
already settled -- take the RAW PAGE SLICE text[first.off : last.off+len(last.text)],
never a re-joined string. Reasons, all checked:
  - fisc verify's fact-offset-points-at-token asserts text[Offset:Offset+len(Token)]
    == Token, so a synthesized "$ -" would fail it while the real slice cannot.
  - "$21130 083" then reaches amount.Parse with its real spacing and splitDigits
    fires, which is the fisc-j5p shape from the other side.
  - CIP p40's "$            -" normalizes to "$ -" and parses as zero, which
    disposes of fisc-yun for free.
  - on a single-word cell the slice is byte-identical to today's token, so
    facts.jsonl does not move.

An empty band raises amount.ErrAbsent naming the cell, wrapped so errors.Is
works. That is NOT the same as reading fisc-8ln's rows: on CIP p40 six cells have
no mark in any substrate, so absent-vs-zero stays fisc-8ln's problem and needs
Rule.TotalColumn beside it.
acceptance_criteria: a sparse row resolves its printed figures to the right columns and raises ErrAbsent naming each cell it has none for; a dense part still gets the exact value count; facts.jsonl is unmoved
notes: 2026-08-18 NOT ON THE CRITICAL PATH for the pp.127-140 / pp.167-170 lanes, measured rather than assumed. All 18 pages in scope were checked against the -bbox geometry in peer review of the landing plan: ZERO rows carry 1-3 value tokens; every data row carries exactly 4, with '-' printed in every zero cell. The only short lines are the running footer. So there is no sparse row for band-driven selection to read, and the exact len(toks)==ExpectedValues guard does not need relaxing for this scope. This note exists because fisc-yun has one and this bead did not, which is one bd ready away from it being re-litigated. Revisit for CIP p40 (fisc-8ln) or any of fisc-gmx's 223 pages.

title: Substrate disagreement: 223 of 786 pages cannot carry the column guard
description:
fisc-yqv.2's guard requires the two substrates to describe the same page: the
same number of non-blank lines, and the same tokens in the same order on each.
Measured over the whole corpus, they do not.

124 of 786 pages disagree on LINE COUNT (59 CIP, 39 budget, 26 ACFR). A further
99 agree on line count and disagree on the TOKENS of some line (89 CIP, 7 budget,
3 ACFR). 223 of 786, 28 percent.

No page in current or near-term mapping scope is among them -- not 66, 67, 127,
128-140, 167-170, CIP 40 or CIP 29 -- and every one of them is REFUSED rather
than read approximately, which is correct. But "the guard is on" and "the page is
readable" will diverge sharply the moment CIP mapping starts, and 89 of the 99
token failures are CIP pages.

TWO CAUSES, both mechanical, and neither is what a first look suggests:

(1) LINE ASSIGNMENT -- 87 of the 89 CIP token failures. A run of words sits on
one line in -layout and on a different line in the geometry clustering. CIP p42
is the worked example: 'Park Fees $2,200,000 ...' is on the PROJECT line in
-layout and on the FUNDING line in geometry.

(2) A SUPERSCRIPT FOOTNOTE MARKER -- the cause on budget pp.68, 70, 186, 190,
192, 194. -layout emits the superscript on its own line; geometry clusters it
into the row. These are financial schedules ONE PAGE from the mapped spine
('Fund Balance by Major and Aggregate Non-Major Funds', 'Available Funds, Uses of
Funds, and Fund Balances'), so this is not a narrative-page problem.

Dot-leader splitting is a minor third case and a TOC phenomenon: budget 3-4,
ACFR 5-6, CIP 3-4 only.

Two pages admit NO tolerance at all: CIP p104 and p111, where the largest
intra-line y0 spread exceeds the smallest inter-line gap (10.57 against 4.43;
7.32 against 6.34). No half-median-height rule reproduces the -layout partition
there, so those need a different grouping or a rule that does not need one.

Do NOT respond by writing a corpus-wide test that asserts 1:1 correspondence. It
is false on 124 pages today.
acceptance_criteria: the two causes are confirmed on a named page each; a rule author can tell from the error which one they hit; the CIP coverage lanes have a cost estimate for it
notes: 2026-08-18 DEFERRED, landing plan. Cite this bead's own sentence rather than re-deriving the conclusion: 'No page in current or near-term mapping scope is among them -- not 66, 67, 127, 128-140, 167-170, CIP 40 or CIP 29.' 223 pages failing the guard matters only when someone maps one of them. Revisit when a coverage bead needs one.

title: data/departments.yaml: a registry for the department axis, and netCells must stop refusing one
description:
Nothing resolves a fact's 'department'. taxonomy.yaml covers categories and funds.yaml covers funds and fund groups; the department axis has no registry at all, so fisc verify's fact-vocabulary check can only report it as unresolvable.

Two separate defects fall out of that, both found in the fisc-1wr.1 peer review:

(1) internal/project's netCells (sankey.go:531-538) REFUSES a fact carrying a department outright. That is correct for the p66-67 spine, which crosses category against fund group and has no department axis -- but it means a department-bearing fact makes check.Load die before any check runs, exiting 1 with no report at all, which is strictly worse than a red check. The refusal needs to become a per-projection error the caller can report, or the projection needs to know the department tier.

(2) fisc-5gk.2 maps Budget Book pp.167-170, department x object category -- roughly 14 departments. Those facts need somewhere to resolve. Until this lands, fisc verify's department axis reports a non-pass with a stated reason rather than a fake pass, which is the honest interim but is exactly the shape that gets a gate commented out if it sits red for long (see fisc-1wr.4's note).

Shape to follow: funds.yaml and taxonomy.yaml both validate on load -- 'a registry that loaded is one whose invariants already hold' (internal/registry/registry.go:1-21). Slugs unique, label required, and the same derived/rationale/source_note discipline for anything editorial. Watch for a slug colliding with a taxonomy category slug; a fact's row_path is department + '/' + category, so a collision is genuinely ambiguous.

Source: the department names printed on pp.167-170 themselves, plus Budget Book pp.255-257 for the fund/department relationship (see the fund-names-come-from-p256 memory -- p253-254 is unreliable for pairing).
acceptance_criteria: every department a fact carries resolves in data/departments.yaml; loading validates; a department-bearing fact produces a reportable per-projection error or a real projection rather than exit 1 with no report; no department slug collides with a taxonomy category slug
notes:
2026-08-18 DESIGN NOTE from reading the pages, landing plan. The axis on pp.167-170 is DIVISION, not department. p0167.txt prints 'City Manager  Wages & Benefits ...' and 'City Clerk  Wages & Benefits ...' as two separate row groups, each with its own Total, under a single 'CITY MANAGER TOTAL'. So the registry needs both levels -- department and the divisions beneath it -- or the joint distribution this bead exists to preserve collapses back into a marginal. This also interacts with fisc-28s Option A: 'one rule per department' may in practice be one rule per division.
2026-08-18 SIZED, from the fisc-28s decision. 11 departments, 22 divisions across pp.167-170. Departments: CITY COUNCIL, CITY MANAGER, CITY ATTORNEY, LIBRARY DEPARTMENT, INNOVATION & ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, GENERAL SERVICES, ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES, POLICE DEPARTMENT, COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, PUBLIC WORKS, FIRE DEPARTMENT. The registry must carry BOTH levels with the parent relation, because Row.Department will hold the division slug (fisc-28s A-prime) while the printed '<DEPARTMENT> TOTAL' line is the department's. Note two departments whose name and sole division's name differ only in case (FIRE DEPARTMENT / Fire Administration; GENERAL SERVICES / General Services), so slug collision is a live hazard within this file as well as against taxonomy.yaml.

title: Tier 1 remainder: the checks that only become non-vacuous after the tier hierarchy lands
description:
fisc-1wr.1 lands in two pieces because three of its checks cannot be non-vacuous at spine-only coverage, and a check reported as passing when it had nothing to test is the exact thing the vacuous status exists to prevent.

Landing with the parent (Wave A): facts sorted; ids unique; every category assignable and every fund_group real; every link's value_cents equals the sum of its fact_ids; graph acyclic; every derived:true node carries rationale + source_note; counts reconcile.

Landing HERE, after fisc-gxa.2:
- AGGREGATION INVARIANCE -- the total at every tier depth equals the total at every other depth. Vacuous today because the shipped graph has one tier depth and there is nothing to fold. Becomes the load-bearing check the instant finest-grain links exist: it is what catches a double-parented or orphaned node.
- constraint_tier is one of the four declared values -- vacuous until any node carries one.

Still vacuous after this and expected to stay so: 'every transfer_id has two equal legs'. No link carries a transfer_id (sankey.go:290-294) and mapping p76 alone does not fix it -- see fisc-4rh.
acceptance_criteria: aggregation invariance runs over more than one tier depth and reports Subjects > 0; constraint-tier membership likewise; the transfer-leg check still reports VACUOUS and is not quietly promoted

title: Fixture expansion: generalise both copies of TestPageFixturesAreVerbatimCopies, add geometry fixtures
description:
testdata/pages/ fixtures are hand-copied from data/extracted/ and the guard that makes every other test in the mapping and build packages mean anything is a byte-comparison against the source. That guard exists TWICE -- internal/mapping/resolve_test.go:96 (hardcoding []int{66,67,127}) and pkg/cmd/build/build_test.go:121 (hardcoding []int{66,67}) -- and both hardcode a single doc id and a single substrate.

Three things it cannot currently express, all of which the PoC needs:
- a second document (CIP p40 for the column guard)
- a second substrate (geometry/pNNNN.json alongside pages/pNNNN.txt)
- the ~17 further page/geometry pairs fisc-5gk.1 (pp.128-140) and fisc-5gk.2 (pp.168-170) require

Make it a table of {doc, artifact path} and cover both substrates. The fixture work is a real cost inside the coverage lanes, not an afterthought -- conventions.md is explicit that a drifted fixture is THE bad case.
acceptance_criteria: one table-driven verbatim-copy test shape covering pages and geometry across all three documents; both existing copies converted; adding a fixture means adding a table row and nothing else
notes:
2026-08-18 THE ACFR GAP IS CLOSED. testdata/pages/acfr-p0177.txt and testdata/geometry/acfr-p0177.json are committed and acfrFixtures joins the table in internal/mapping/resolve_test.go, so the verbatim-copy guard now covers all THREE documents -- which was the AC clause holding this open. The fixture is there for a named failure mode, per testdata/README.md's standing rule, and in fact for two: the page behind the project's most-cited arithmetic claim (whose quoted token turned out to be an xberg artefact), and a live fisc-yun standalone '$'.

STILL OPEN, and now the only thing holding this bead: the ~17 further page/geometry pairs pp.128-140 and pp.168-170 need. Those are deliberately NOT bulk-copied. README's rule is that each fixture names the failure mode it is there for, and 'a generic sample' is exactly what a bulk copy would be -- they should land with the lane that needs them (fisc-5gk.1 / fisc-5gk.2), each with its reason, not in advance of it. Note neither lane is blocked on the fixtures alone: fisc-5gk.1 still needs fisc-u2v, which is a decision.

title: Row identity for the department x object pages: one rule per department, or Part.Department
description:
Row.Department is per-RULE, but on Budget Book pp.167-170 the department varies per PART while the category rows (Wages & Benefits, Services & Supplies, Total) repeat -- and parse.go:226 requires row labels to be unique within a rule. So a single rule CANNOT cover ten departments.

Option A -- one rule per department (~14 rules). Works with today's schema, no Go change. Fact ids stay distinct because rule_id is in MakeID's tuple. Cost: 14 near-identical rule blocks in the mapping file.

Option B -- a new Part.Department that qualifies its rows. Cleaner file, but mapping.Value must then carry the department through into fact.FromValues, which is a change to the value/fact seam.

Recommendation: A. Decide BEFORE fisc-0cs lands, because the choice determines what a p167 part's section/stop_at anchors look like and therefore what the continuation fixtures are testing.
acceptance_criteria: the decision is recorded here with its reasoning; fisc-5gk.2 and fisc-0cs both reference it; if B is chosen, the Value->Fact seam change is scoped in this bead
notes:
2026-08-18 DECIDED: neither A nor B as written. Take A-PRIME -- ONE RULE PER
DIVISION, 22 of them. No Go change. Evidence from reading pp.167-170.

WHY OPTION A AS WRITTEN IS IMPOSSIBLE, NOT MERELY VERBOSE

parse.go:227-235 builds rowIndex over r.Rows -- unique per RULE -- and every
Part of a rule shares that one row set. A department is not the unit that has a
unique row set: ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES (p168:15-35) contains three divisions,
Administrative Services, Finance and Human Resources, and each prints the SAME
three labels Wages & Benefits / Services & Supplies / Total. One rule per
department is three duplicate labels, refused at parse time. The bead's estimate
of "~14 rules" also undercounts: there are 11 departments and 22 divisions.

AND THE ROW SET IS NOT EVEN UNIFORM ACROSS DIVISIONS

- FIRE DEPARTMENT (p170:13-19) has one division, Fire Administration, printing
  only Services & Supplies and Total -- NO Wages & Benefits row.
- General Services (p167:63 - p168:13) prints a fourth label, Debt Services.

So a single shared row set spanning divisions fails on both. The division is the
smallest unit whose row set is self-consistent, which is what makes it the rule
boundary.

WHY NOT OPTION B

B (Part.Department qualifying its rows) would need the qualifier to be the
DIVISION, not the department -- the department is a grouping above it -- and it
still costs the mapping.Value -> fact.FromValues seam change the bead flags. A'
gets the same facts with no Go change. Fact ids stay distinct because rule_id is
in MakeID's tuple.

WHERE THE DEPARTMENT GOES

Row.Department (per rule) carries the DIVISION slug. The department/division
hierarchy lives in data/departments.yaml (fisc-o15), which has to model both
levels regardless -- see the design note added there on this date. The all-caps
department heading and the "<DEPARTMENT> TOTAL" line become the anchor context
and the stated total for the department's divisions taken together.

TWO SHAPES THE RULE AUTHOR WILL HIT

(1) ONE DIVISION SPANS A PAGE BREAK. General Services prints its Wages &
Benefits row as the last line of p167 and its Services & Supplies, Debt Services
and Total rows at the head of p168. That division's rule needs two Parts on two
pages, with the rows split between them. Every other division is single-page;
the department-level breaks (GENERAL SERVICES p167->p168, POLICE p168->p169,
PUBLIC WORKS p169->p170) fall between divisions except this one.

(2) THE CONTINUATION FRAGMENTS ARE DIVISION LABELS, NOT STRAY TEXT. This
sharpens fisc-0cs. Exactly four across the four pages, and each is the second
line of a wrapped DIVISION NAME:
    p0167:56  Devel              (Innovation & Economic Devel)
    p0169:16  Development Admin
    p0169:34  Services
    p0169:50  Administration
Correction to fisc-0cs's description: it says "more on p170" -- there are none
on p170. So the fragment is part of the row's own identity, which is an argument
for Row.Continuation over a bare checkGap relaxation: the two lines together are
the label.
close_reason: Decided A-prime: ONE RULE PER DIVISION, 22 of them, no Go change. Option A as written (one rule per department) is impossible rather than merely verbose -- parse.go:227-235 makes row labels unique per RULE and every Part shares one row set, while ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES holds three divisions each printing the same three labels. The row set is not uniform either: Fire Administration prints no Wages & Benefits row and General Services prints a fourth label, Debt Services, so the division is the smallest unit whose row set is self-consistent. Option B would need the qualifier to be the division anyway and still costs the Value->Fact seam change. Row.Department carries the division slug; the department/division hierarchy lives in data/departments.yaml (fisc-o15, sized on the same date: 11 departments, 22 divisions). Two shapes recorded for the rule author: General Services splits mid-division across the p167/p168 break and needs two Parts, and the four continuation fragments are wrapped division LABELS rather than stray text, which sharpened fisc-0cs toward Row.Continuation. Full reasoning in the notes.

title: sankey.json schema_version 2: finest-grain links, and page.go must refuse an unknown version
description:
fisc-gxa.2 changes what `links` MEANS: today a revenue-source -> fund-group link is the whole flow; after the tier migration it is a leaf the client must fold. A v1 consumer reading a v2 file draws a chart that is WRONG, not one that fails, so the version has to move and the reader has to gate on it.

Two halves:
(1) project.SchemaVersion 1 -> 2, and docs/sankey-contract.md updated to describe finest-grain links plus node.parent/node.tier.
(2) internal/export/page.go currently copies doc.SchemaVersion straight into FISC_CONFIG (page.go:212) with NO validation anywhere in the package -- while internal/corpus, internal/registry and internal/mapping all gate theirs. Close that gap in the same change.

The contract was frozen in its own commit precisely so producer, packager and consumer could be built concurrently against it. Changing it is a decision, not a bullet inside another bead -- same precedent as fisc-j8f (YAML) and fisc-zna (d3).

title: Printed dashes missing from the PDF text layer on some CIP rows
description:
On CIP p40 the rendered page PRINTS '-' in the intervening FY columns of rows PB200654 and PB202617, but those dashes are in NO substrate: absent from pdftotext -layout, -raw, default mode, and from the -bbox geometry. They are drawn as non-text in the PDF. Row PB200429 on the same page DOES carry its dashes, so this is per-row, not a flag choice. The old xberg artifacts lacked them too, so it is not a regression -- but it is a real limitation of the corpus that the fail-closed rule needs an answer for.

Why it matters: 'absent is not zero' is a load-bearing invariant. A printed '-' is a zero FACT; an empty cell means the line does not apply. On these rows the two are indistinguishable from any artifact, and extraction currently offers no channel to signal 'unrecognised' so a consumer can fail closed.

Options to weigh: (a) detect the gap via geometry -- a column position with no token between two tokens that do have positions -- and emit an explicit 'unknown' marker rather than nothing; (b) require rules over affected pages to declare the shape; (c) render-based detection. Do NOT resolve it by defaulting a missing token to zero.

Found in peer review of fisc-yqv.3.
acceptance_criteria: a rule over CIP p40 reads PB200654 correctly; no path silently treats an absent token as zero
notes:
2026-08-18 AC TIGHTENED when fisc-yqv.2 landed. It used to read "either reads
PB200654 correctly OR fails closed with a message naming the missing cell" --
and the column guard now satisfies the or-branch, which would have left "reads
correctly" as the obligation of no open bead. The or-branch is deleted; this bead
owns reading the row.

Interim state, verified by TestCIPp40SparseRowFailsClosedButDoesNotRead: the read
runs off the end of the row's two printed figures and into the row-label area and
is refused naming the row and the column. The test is named for what it proves.
Nothing is filed under the wrong year.

title: Continuation rows: wrapped labels land between a row's figures and the next label
description:
pdftotext -layout wraps long department names onto a second line that lands BETWEEN a row's last figure and the next row's label:

  Innovation & Economic Wages & Benefits   1,028,282  1,068,663  1,233,502  1,192,014
  Devel
                        Services & Supplies  1,610,950  2,592,436  2,870,310  2,829,666

Occurrences on the department pages: p167 'Devel'; p169 'Development Admin', 'Services', 'Administration'; more on p170.

checkGap (resolve.go:394) rejects any non-whitespace between rows, so these pages cannot be read. skip: true CANNOT express it -- a skipped row still consumes ncols tokens and these fragments have zero.

Needs either a Row.Continuation concept or a principled checkGap relaxation. Both are exactly the kind of change 'fail closed' makes expensive to get right, so it needs its own bead rather than being absorbed into a coverage lane.

xberg did not hit this because it fused everything onto one line -- which is also why it lost the rows. The two defects are the same defect from opposite sides.

BLOCKS fisc-5gk.2 (GF department x object, pp.167-170).
acceptance_criteria: pp.167-170 resolve with the correct row count and no relaxation of the unmapped-row check for non-continuation text
notes: 2026-08-18 A SECOND LANE NOW PAYS THIS. The bug is not confined to the department pages: Budget Book p0076.txt:351 prints 'Connection' on its own line, the wrapped tail of 'Transfer From Wastewater to LAVWMA / Wastewater Connection', landing between that row's figures and the next row's label -- the exact shape enumerated for pp.167-170. checkGap refuses it, so the p76 reconciliation (fisc-5gk.3) has to split the Enterprise section into two parts around it. That workaround is available to a reconciliation because part boundaries are declared; it is not a fix, and fisc-5gk.3.1 should not have to ship it. Row.Continuation would serve p76 as well as the department pages: here too the two lines together are the label.

title: Delete the table substrate and the markdown residue
description:

title: StatedTotals cannot read a label-less totals row that shares a line
description:
Budget Book p67's expenditure totals row and its TRANSFER OUT: row extract onto
ONE physical line:

  ... $1,061,355 ... $26,544,515 28,584,740 36,047,736 - - 1,137,050 900,550 40,000 612,000

StatedTotals reads a label-less part's totals as the first MAXIMAL run of
consecutively parsable amounts on the anchor's line and requires that run to be
exactly one per column. Here the run is 16 amounts, not 8, so
CheckTotals(spine-expenditures, p67) returns ErrNotFound and eight columns of
the published spine go unchecked by the document's own total. No stop_at fixes
it from the rule file: blk.End is already at the first totals token; the problem
is the shape of the line after it. (The revenue half of p67 ties only because
its totals row happens to end its line.)

FIX: for a label-less part, blk.End is BY CONSTRUCTION the first token of the
totals row, so the totals are the first n consecutively parsable amounts from
that exact offset. The maximal-run rule exists to stop a totals LABEL containing
a bare number ("Total 2022 COP Construction Fund") from being read as a figure,
which can only happen on the labelled path -- so keep the maximal-run rule where
LabelsFrom == 0 and take the first n where it is set.

Then in internal/mapping/mappings_test.go: delete
TestP67ExpenditureTotalsCannotBeRead, set spineTiedColumns to 24, and drop
"spine-expenditures p67" from the unchecked list in TestPublishedSpineResolves.
Those eight columns are currently tied instead by
TestPublishedSpineBalancesPerFundGroup, which reconciles all six fund groups in
both years against the city's printed TOTAL SOURCES / TOTAL USES rows.
close_reason: Duplicate of fisc-gxt, filed independently for the same defect within minutes. Fixed there. Note the fix taken differs from the one proposed here: rather than dropping the maximal-run requirement for label-less parts, amountRun now also considers a run's $-PREFIXED prefix when the maximal run is the wrong width. That keeps the maximal-run guard on both paths and uses the distinction the document itself draws -- totals rows are $-marked, data rows bare -- instead of trusting blk.End's position.

title: Labelled read cannot handle a standalone $ token
description:
amount.Parse("$") is an error ('no digits, only currency or bracket characters'), and 246 of 786 corpus pages emit $ as its own whitespace-delimited token: 'Total Uses 6/30/24 $ 123,228,190 $ 14,507,398'. The labelled read takes the next N whitespace-delimited tokens after a row label, so on those pages it reads [$, 123,228,190, $, 14,507,398] and fails.

pp.66-67 contain zero standalone $ tokens, so fisc-mq4.2 is unaffected and the failure is closed, not silent. But the labelled read is described as the general text mode and is not yet general.

Do NOT fix by making amount.Parse accept a bare $ -- that would weaken the fail-closed grammar. The join belongs in the resolver's tokenizer, which knows it is looking for N amounts and can merge a currency-only token with the one that follows it.
acceptance_criteria: A page whose rows print '$ 1,234' resolves; amount.Parse still rejects a bare $; a token that is currency-only and NOT followed by an amount is still an error.
notes: 2026-08-18 A REAL PAGE NOW SHOWS IT, and it is committed. ACFR p177's FY2016 row prints '$ 60,193,384' -- the dollar sign as its OWN token before each of its eight figures, while the nine rows beneath it print bare numbers. So the standalone-$ shape is not hypothetical and not confined to pages out of scope: it makes ACFR p177 unreadable by the resolver, which is why internal/mapping/acfr_p177_test.go parses that page with strings.Fields instead of a rule and says so. The memory scope-pages-are-dense ('zero standalone $ tokens') was measured over Budget Book pp.127-140 and 167-170 and remains true of them; it was never a statement about the ACFR. title: Declared per-part allowance for the document's own rounding
description:
The spine ties exactly, but 'all totals tie exactly' is NOT a property of this corpus and must not be hardened into one. A correct label-anchored read of Budget Book p127 Total Property Taxes gives 58,179,467 against a printed 58,179,468. Ten more blocks are off by |delta| <= $5, every one in the FY2023-24 Actual column: pp. 111, 128, 129, 131, 135, 168, 172, 173, 181, 183. Verified by hand on p127 (the other three columns tie exactly) and p129/p172.

This is rounding in the DOCUMENT, not in the read. CheckTotals currently demands exact equality, so mapping stalls at p127 on a correct read.

Wanted: a per-part 'stated_total_delta' the rule author writes down and justifies -- never a silent tolerance, and never a global epsilon. The declaration is the point: it records that a human looked at the discrepancy and found it to be the city's rounding.
acceptance_criteria: A rule can declare an expected discrepancy for one part; CheckTotals accepts exactly that delta and no other; an undeclared discrepancy still fails; p127 maps with the delta declared.
close_reason:
Landed. stated_total_deltas on Part: a per-column, per-page declaration of a discrepancy in the DOCUMENT's own arithmetic. No global epsilon, no per-rule fuzz.

SHAPE. StatedTotalDelta{Column (1-based, matching how CheckTotals numbers columns when it reports a mismatch, so a failure message can be pasted into a declaration), Cents (STATED MINUS MAPPED, in cents always), Note (required)}. The parser refuses an out-of-range column, a duplicate column, a skipped column, a zero delta and a missing or whitespace-only note -- so a malformed declaration fails when the file is READ, not when it is applied.

BEHAVIOUR. CheckTotals accepts exactly the declared figure and nothing else. Three failure modes, told apart in the message: an undeclared discrepancy fails as before; a declared column off by a different amount fails naming both figures; and a declared column that now TIES EXACTLY also fails, telling the author to remove the declaration. That last one is the direction nothing else would catch -- if the city reissues the page with the arithmetic corrected, a tolerance would silently keep passing while the declaration became a false claim about the document.

THE ARITHMETIC, carried in the test rather than described. Budget Book p127's thirteen Property Taxes rows, from the committed fixture: FY2023-24 Actual 58,179,467 against a printed 58,179,468 (+1); FY2024-25 60,621,418, FY2025-26 64,143,762, FY2026-27 67,416,730, all exact. Three of four columns tying exactly is what makes the fourth the document's rounding rather than our read -- a misread row would not land on three columns and miss one by a dollar.

REPORTING. TotalsResult.Declared and Report.ColumnsTiedByDeclaration, printed whenever non-zero: '1 of those columns ties only to a declared delta in the document's own arithmetic'. A column that ties on the city's rounding must not be counted as one that ties exactly; that is the same principle as pkg/cmd/build/report.go's UNCHECKED lines.

TESTS. 5 test functions, 12 subtests, over the real p127 fixture rather than a synthetic page. All proven failable by mutation: neutering the CheckTotals branch reddens the three behaviour tests, neutering the parser loop reddens the two refusal tests. The report test caught a real grammar bug on the way in ('1 of those column tie'), now fixed by pluralising the verb rather than the noun.

title: Verify a label-less continuation part against its own totals
description:
Raised by code review of the rule schema and deferred, not fixed.

A rule's total_row is matched by LABEL, but a continuation part carries no labels at all -- Budget Book p67's totals row is positional like everything else on that page. So the single most valuable check available (the document checking our work) currently cannot run on exactly the pages that most need it, since a label-less page is also the one where a positional read is most fragile.

Resolve before or with the resolver. Options worth weighing: give Part its own optional total spec (a positional index, or 'the first line whose figures are $-prefixed', which is how p67 actually reads); or treat the continuation's totals row as an extra positional row with a reserved label. Whichever is chosen, the assertion must be per-column: p67 prints four fund-group totals ($27,145,882 / $0 / $28,465,560 / $18,969,834 for FY2026), and the M0 spike confirmed all four tie exactly.
close_reason: CheckTotals asserts per column and is production-callable, not test-only. A label-less part reads its stated totals from the stop_at boundary, which is how p67 prints them ('$' is both the block terminator and the first character of $27,145,882). StatedTotals takes the first maximal run of exactly one-amount-per-column within the anchor's line: maximal because totals labels contain bare numbers, exact because a doubled totals line must fail rather than guess, line-bound because the next row's figures would extend the run. All four p67 fund-group columns tie.

title: pages.yml deploy
description:
On push to main: checkout WITHOUT LFS (the site does not need the PDFs), fisc build, fisc export -o dist --clean, upload-pages-artifact, deploy-pages. Actions pinned by SHA.

Keeping LFS out of CI matters: data/pdf/** is the ONLY thing in LFS (3 files, ~67MB) and GitHub's free tier is 1GB/month of bandwidth, so ~14 LFS checkouts exhaust it. data/extracted/ is ordinary git, so a no-LFS checkout still carries everything fisc reads.

Consequence for the frontend, in two parts:
- The PDFs ARE in LFS, so raw.githubusercontent.com serves pointer text for them. PDF deep links must therefore target the city's canonical URL with #page=N.
- The extracted page text is NOT in LFS and raw would serve it correctly. Citations still point at the github.com BLOB view, for a different reason: the blob view has line numbers, history and the rest of the document beside it, and the artifacts are pages/pNNNN.txt -- .txt, not .md, since fisc-yqv -- precisely so that view renders them verbatim instead of collapsing the runs of spaces that ARE the column grid.
notes:
2026-08-17 (from lane A4, fisc-1wr.5): `fisc verify --full` now exists and is the only thing in the project that reads data/pdf/. It recomputes each PDF's sha256 and compares it against BOTH data/sources.yaml and the extraction manifest. A monthly scheduled workflow for it is this bead's, deliberately not added in A4.

Two things that job must get right: it needs `lfs: true` AND must not inherit GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE (ci.yml sets it workflow-wide, so a new workflow file is cleaner than a job in ci.yml), because a pointer-only checkout makes the check report ERROR ('an unsmudged Git LFS pointer ... run `git lfs pull`') rather than a false failure -- correct, but it means the job would never actually hash anything. 1. link.kind gains a FOURTH value: {external, internal_transfer, internal_service, fund_balance}. A fund-balance draw or contribution is not external money and must not enter the headline, and labelling it internal_transfer would be false -- it is not a transfer between funds, it is a fund drawing on or adding to its own accumulated balance. Explicit fund-balance-draw / fund-balance-contribution nodes were already required by this bead; they need a link kind of their own.

The published stock rows (fund-balance/beginning, /ending) are facts but are excluded from the graph as stocks rather than flows, and metadata.caveats must say so.
